vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: skywork-music-maker
Version: 1.0.3

The skywork-music-maker skill bundle is a legitimate tool for generating music via the Mureka AI API. The Python script (scripts/mureka.py) implements standard API interactions, including file uploads and polling for generation tasks, while the documentation (SKILL.md, README.md) provides clear instructions for the AI agent to assist users with music production workflows without any evidence of malicious intent or data exfiltration.

llm.summary: The skill's code and docs clearly require and use a MUREKA_API_KEY and upload user audio to https://api.mureka.ai, but the registry metadata does not declare any required environment variables or provenance — this mismatch and missing transparency merit caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name and description (AI music generator) align with its code and SKILL.md: the Python CLI talks to https://api.mureka.ai to generate songs, instrumentals, lyrics, and to upload reference/vocal files. However, the registry metadata claims 'Required env vars: none' while both SKILL.md and scripts/mureka.py require MUREKA_API_KEY. Not declaring the API key in metadata is an incoherence and reduces transparency about needed credentials.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to convert user text into structured prompts, validate them, request confirmation, then call the Mureka API. The instructions are focused on music generation workflows and reference uploading user-provided audio files (vocal/reference/melody). The instructions do not ask the agent to read unrelated system files or exfiltrate arbitrary data. They do, however, instruct uploading local files to the external API when the user requests that feature — expected for this purpose but privacy-relevant.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only + an included script). No downloads or external installers are defined. The included Python script is straightforward and uses the requests library to interact with the API. This is low install risk, but users should review the provided script before running it.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires a single external credential (MUREKA_API_KEY) to operate, which is proportionate to the stated purpose. The problem is the registry metadata did not declare any required env vars or a primary credential — an inconsistency. Also, the skill will upload local audio files and send lyrics/prompts to an external API; users should understand that uploaded audio and prompt text will be transmitted to the third-party service.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true, does not modify other skills' configurations, and is not installing persistent system components. It runs as a CLI wrapper around the remote API and stores outputs in local directories specified by the user (normal behavior).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says (convert prompts and call the Mureka AI API), but there are important transparency and privacy issues to consider before installing:

- The README and SKILL.md require a MUREKA_API_KEY and will upload files and prompts to https://api.mureka.ai, but the registry metadata did not declare that environment variable. Treat that as a red flag: ask the publisher or registry maintainer to correct the metadata so required credentials are explicit.
- Uploaded files (reference tracks, vocal samples) and prompts/lyrics are sent to an external service. Do not upload private, sensitive, or copyrighted third-party audio unless you understand Mureka's terms and privacy policy.
- Review scripts/mureka.py yourself before use (it is short and readable). Confirm the API base (api.mureka.ai) is the intended endpoint and verify the service's reputation and privacy/billing policies.
- Prefer using a scoped API key with minimal permissions and monitor its use. If you want to limit exposure, run the skill in a sandboxed environment and avoid uploading sensitive files.

What would change this assessment: if the registry metadata were corrected to list MUREKA_API_KEY (and ideally a homepage/owner identity and provenance), and the publisher had a known/trustworthy source, the rating would likely be benign. Conversely, if additional undisclosed endpoints, obfuscated code, or undeclared credentials were found, the rating would escalate.
